resources.name: Authorization Tokens

actions.name: Create an Authorization Token
actions.description:
Create a new authorization token for an authenticated user. This authorization token may be used to access protected resources.

Example:

$ curl -i \
  --request POST \
  --user "test@test.test:testtest" \
  --data-urlencode "tokenDescription=What's this token for?" \
  https://api.apiary.io/authorization
$ curl -i \
  --request POST \
  --user "test@test.test:testtest" \
  --data-urlencode "tokenDescription=What's this token for?" \
  --data-urlencode "tokenRegenerate=true" \
  https://api.apiary.io/authorization

actions.name: Get Existing Authorization Tokens
actions.description:
Get existing authorization tokens for an authenticated user. These authorization tokens may be used to access protected resources.

Example:

$ curl -i \
  --request GET \
  --user "test@test.test:testtest" \
  https://api.apiary.io/authorization

actions.name: Delete an Existing Authorization Token
actions.description:
Delete an existing authorization token for an authenticated user. This authorization token may no longer be used to access protected resources.

Example:

$ curl -i \
  --request DELETE \
  --user "test@test.test:testtest" \
  --data-urlencode "tokenDescription=What's this token for?" \
  https://api.apiary.io/authorization
$ curl -i \
  --request DELETE \
  --user "test@test.test:testtest" \
  https://api.apiary.io/authorization/What%27s%20this%20token%20for%3F

resources.description: This resource represents a collection of authorization tokens granted to an Apiary API user. This collection works only for users who are not part of the IDCS controlled teams.

resourceGroups.name: User Information
resourceGroups.description:
Apiary API exposes authorized user information.

  1. You may only get your own user information.

  2. You may use your authorization token to access your protected information.

    Authorization: Bearer 874887d6ecd0b106a47448c5beca1...

  3. You must use encryption (i.e., HTTPS).

resources.name: Me

actions.name: Get Me
actions.description:
Get your user information. A valid authorization token must be used to access this information.

Example:

$ curl -i \
  --request GET \
  --header "authorization:bearer 874887d6ecd0b106a47448c5beca1..." \
  https://api.apiary.io/me

resources.description: This resource represents you as an Apiary API user.

resourceGroups.name: API List
resourceGroups.description:
Apiary API exposes lists of APIs.

  1. You may only get your own user information.

  2. You may use your authorization token to access private and public, personal and team APIs.

    Authorization: Bearer 874887d6ecd0b106a47448c5beca1...

  3. You must use encryption (i.e., HTTPS).

resources.name: User API List

actions.name: Get User API List
actions.description:
Get a list of public and private, personal and team APIs an authorized user may access. A valid authorization token must be used to access this information.

Example:

$ curl -i \
  --request GET \
  --header "authorization:bearer 874887d6ecd0b106a47448c5beca1..." \
  https://api.apiary.io/me/apis

resources.name: Team API List

actions.description:

Example:

$ curl -i \
  --request GET \
  --header "authorization:bearer 874887d6ecd0b106a47448c5beca1..." \

resources.description: This resource represents a list of team APIs an Apiary API user may access. The list may contain public or private, team APIs.

resourceGroups.name: Blueprint
resourceGroups.description:
Apiary API exposes legacy API Blueprint utilities.

You may use our legacy, authorization token HTTP header (i.e., Authentication: Token 874887d6ecd0b106a47448c5beca1...) to publish an API Blueprint for a particular API.

actions.name: Create API Project
actions.description: If the desiredName is already taken, a different domain will be generated for your API Project. It can be later changed in the settings.

actions.name: Fetch Blueprint
actions.description: Fetch an API Blueprint for a particular API. Our legacy, authorization token HTTP header (i.e., Authentication: Token 874887d6ecd0b106a47448c5beca1...) with a valid authorization token must be used to access this utility.

actions.name: Publish Blueprint
actions.description:
Publish an API Blueprint for a particular API. Our legacy, authorization token HTTP header (i.e., Authentication: Token 874887d6ecd0b106a47448c5beca1...) with a valid authorization token must be used to access this utility.

Example:

$ curl -i \
  --request POST \
  --header "Authentication:Token 874887d6ecd0b106a47448c5beca1..." \
  --header "content-type:application/json; charset=utf-8" \
  --data-binary @- \
  https://api.apiary.io/blueprint/publish/publicpersonalapi \
<<EOF
{ "code": "FORMAT: X-1A\nHOST: http://api.example.com/\n\n# Example API\n\nIntroduction." }
EOF
